  "text": "In the spring, Maren had the eleventh tread repaired.

The joiner came on a Tuesday with his tools wrapped in a towel. He worked until noon. When he finished, he asked her to try it.

She went up and came down.

"That'll outlast us," he said.

She paid him from the harbour account and entered the sum beside the purchase of a new rain gauge. For several nights afterward, her foot lifted too high at that place in the stair.

Erris no longer waited every evening. There were examinations, then a job at the shop, then a boy from the other side of the headland who brought her home on a motorbike. Maren heard them sometimes as she put on her coat. The engine stopped outside the Kessocks' house. After a while it started again.

She was glad the girl had other things to do.

One morning she found a shopping list in the back of Agnes's log. Flour. Soap. Two oranges. The writing was smaller than the entries at the front, hurried and slanting toward the edge.

Maren sat with it until the kettle boiled dry.

She had remembered her mother standing at the window, listening. She had forgotten the oranges, how Agnes cut them into quarters and left them on a blue plate between their chairs.

That afternoon she bought two.

At midnight the plate was still on the table. She covered it before going out.

The new tread made no sound beneath her foot. Above it, the stair continued. She climbed, carrying the key in her pocket."
